lead: Berkshire Hathaway Class B / BRK-B — Buffett's letter lands in a war market
smaller: Rheinmetall / RHM.DE — Germany becomes the war trade's buyer
Block / SQ — the beaten fintech jumps by a quarter
MP Materials / MP — rare earths become a security trade
why_lead: Buffett's annual letter (26 February) is the weekend's densest retail-attention cluster and a narrative never used in any earlier retail edition: record $27 billion buybacks with surging operating earnings (CNBC n0806), the lament about a lack of good investments (Reuters n0807), Apple as one of the Four Giants (CNBC n0828), the attack on fake earnings (Business Insider n0826), the 'mildly attractive' buyback path (Time n0827), $89.8B net profit (n0837), plus retail-facing follow-ons (MoneyWise portfolio changes n0738, Yahoo Finance's 'fourth law of motion' n0876, CNBC's panic-sell guide n1969). Own-card move: BRK-B 319.24 USD, +3.56% 1-session, +1.81% 5-session vs S&P 500 +0.10%, +3.76% 20-session vs +1.34%; Apple 164.85 USD +1.30%; VIX 27.59 (-2.73 pts) (prior close 2022-02-25). Simple, repeatable story: in a war market, buy the investor who stays calm. Split view comes from the letter itself (no good investments, buybacks only mildly attractive) against the bull reading of record buybacks and the Four Giants. Chronology: chosen over a second consecutive defence lead. Defence ran as smaller items on 2022-02-22 and 2022-02-24 and as the 2022-02-25 lead; Germany's €100 billion pledge is new evidence but is carried as a smaller item to keep four distinct narratives. The Buffett-avoids-Russia headline (n0393) was also cited in the 2022-02-24 ITA item; here it supports the analog only.
why_smaller: Rheinmetall / RHM.DE: material update of the defence family (2022-02-22 LMT smaller item, 2022-02-24 ITA smaller item, 2022-02-25 ITA lead) with decisive new weekend evidence: Germany commits €100 billion to defence (DW n1228), Scholz's response to 'Putin's war' (Reuters n1229), POLITICO's historic shift (n1230), BBC's dramatic U-turn (n1232). Card: Rheinmetall 107.05 EUR, +7.00% 1-session, +11.00% 5-session, +15.06% 20-session from 93.04 EUR; LMT +3.48% to 409.49 USD, RTX +4.11%. The Fortune WallStreetBets headline (n0623) is cited only as context for the earlier crowd reaction.

Block / SQ: a distinct results-day comeback narrative and the card's largest one-session gain among US stocks: 119.82 USD, +26.14% 1-session, +15.19% 5-session, +13.42% 20-session from 105.64 USD, PayPal +5.64% (prior close 2022-02-25); evidence is the results-call marketing-spend headline (Payments Dive n1073), ABC's Block-soars-on-the-ASX report (n0061) and CNBC's company profile (n0584). Block has not appeared in earlier retail editions; fintech peers SoFi (2022-02-23), Affirm (2022-02-14) and PayPal (2022-02-02, -03) did, so the item focuses on Block's own print and notes peers only as breaks (PayPal -29.83%, Affirm -23.17% over 20 sessions).

MP Materials / MP: a distinct supply-chain-security narrative not used in earlier retail editions: higher profit as rare-earth prices surge (Reuters n0595), the Department of Defense heavy rare-earth processing contract (n0341) and the chip-shortage warning (n1965); card MP 46.85 USD, +6.84% 1-session, +12.62% 5-session, +25.10% 20-session from 37.45 USD, Lynas +6.93% to 9.57 AUD.
considered_not_chosen: Russian equity ETFs after SWIFT (Seeking Alpha Russia ETF explainer n1820, NYT SWIFT n1412, Global Finance n1226, Tinkoff n1975, BP's Rosneft exit n0836): strong weekend catalyst but no Russian instrument on the card, and Monday's Moscow reopening is after the cutoff; SWIFT is used as backdrop in the lead instead.

Bitcoin / BTC-USD (37,709.79 USD, -3.57% on 27 February, -13.98% over 20 observations; BBC on donations n0948, Peirce on a spot ETF n0949): crypto already ran on 4, 8, 9, 14, 15, 21 and 25 February; no distinct crowd catalyst with a price reaction.
Wheat / ZW=F reversal (843.00 US cents/bu, -8.96% 1-session but +5.64% 5-session): a round trip of the 2022-02-24 item without a new crowd angle.
GameStop / GME ('Gaming Wall Street' trailer coverage n0127, n0847; GME -4.82%): meme nostalgia already covered by the 2022-02-23 AMC item.
Carvana (+21.04% with the ADESA deal) and Opendoor (-23.13% after results), Dell (-7.84% on a miss, n0714), Zscaler (-15.77%): large moves but weaker crowd evidence than Block.

3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ (51.91 USD, +4.74%) and the panic-sell-regret story (CNBC n1969, Seeking Alpha n1947): the leveraged dip-buy ran on 4, 11, 22, 24 and 25 February; n1969 is used in the lead's Social Signal instead.
Polish banks' Friday rebound (Pekao +17.14%, PKO +13.27%): a Poland-section story without retail-attention evidence.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff: n1971 (excluded; Bank of Russia block on foreign clients' sales, reported around the Monday Moscow open). No Bank of Russia rate decision, Monday ruble move or Moscow exchange closure was used; no Sunday-stamped item describing Monday trading was cited.
